paragraphs.text: Tint the DSH web UI with the KDE system accent color.
# dsh-kde-tint

> [!WARNING]
> Personal-use project. It is built and tested for my own machine and workflow only; I
do not guarantee it works on other DSH versions, platforms or setups. Review the code first and use
it at your own risk.
Tint the DSH web UI with the KDE system accent color.
## Background
The DSH web UI ships a neutral theme. On a KDE desktop the user already picks a color scheme. This p
lugin reads the **currently applied** colors and tints the DSH interface with them. The harness then
matches the desktop.
The plugin has two halves. The host half (`lib/index.js`) reads the `Colors:*` sections that Plasma
writes to `~/.config/kdeglobals`; on Material You / dynamic-color setups those sections carry the li
ve palette, while the `.colors` file on disk can be stale. It serves the result as JSON from the pro
file web server. The browser half (`lib/client.js`) fetches the JSON and applies the tint through th
e `theme` service. The two halves talk over plain HTTP. A static client bundle has no host bridge, s
o HTTP is the correct channel.
The tint accent is `Colors:Selection.BackgroundNormal` (the applied selection color), not `General.A
ccentColor`, which often stays at an old manual value. `Colors:Window`, `Colors:View` and `Colors:Bu
tton` seed the surface ramp: the deepest canvas, the panel layer and the raised layer.
On systems without KDE configuration the plugin falls back to the active color-scheme file, then to
defaults (accent `#386798`, scheme `MaterialYouDark`). It never blocks startup because of a missing
cent `#386798`, scheme `MaterialYouDark`). It never blocks startup because of a missing config file.

Then open the DSH web UI. Surfaces, controls, borders and scrollbars carry the applied KDE palette.
## Usage
The plugin needs no clicks. It loads with `immediately: true` and tints the UI on every page load. U
ninstall (or disable) restores the stock theme. The token override is effect-scoped, so it unwinds w
sable) restores the stock theme. The token override is effect-scoped, so it unwinds with the plugin.
Upgrading from 0.2.x changes the host half as well, so restart `dsh web` once; after that a page ref
0.2.x changes the host half as well, so restart `dsh web` once; after that a page refresh is enough.
### What gets tinted
The client builds a light and a dark palette from the applied scheme and overrides 57 DSH tokens. Su
rfaces mix 10–24% of the accent into the scheme's own base colors, so the UI keeps the desktop's dep
th instead of washing out. When the scheme is dark, `Colors:View` becomes the canvas, `Colors:Window
` the sidebar, and `Colors:Button` the raised layers; a light scheme seeds the light palette the sam
e way, and the other mode falls back to a neutral base plus accent.
| Group | Tokens |
| Surfaces | `bg-base`, `bg-layer-1/2/3`, `sidebar-fill`, `bg-overlay`, `bg-document-preview`, `bg-s

keleton` |
| Message bubbles | `specific-bubble`, `specific-bubble-highlight` |
| Raised panels | `b
g-module-platform`, `specific-input-major`, menu surfaces, `markdown-code-block` (+ banner, inline c

ode, tag) |
| State fills | `interactive-bg-hover` / `-active` / `-hover-solid` |
| Neutral controls
| `button-elevated-fill`, `button-floating-fill` / `-hover`, `button-ghost-active-fill` / `-border`

, `button-contrast-fill`, `button-tool-bar-fill` / `-hover`, `specific-selector`, `switch-thumb` |
|

Navigation | `specific-sidebar-nav-item-hover` / `-active` |
| Borders | `border-l1` … `border-l4`,

`border-l2-darkmode-thin` |
| Scrollbars | `scrollbar-bg-l1` / `-l2`, `scrollbar-hover-l1` / `-l2`

|
| Brand | `brand-primary` (raw selection accent), `button-primary-hover`, `button-primary-dimmed`

|
| Toast / tooltip | `tooltip-bg`, `toast-bg` |
| Onboarding | `onboarding-card-fill`, `onboarding-
secondary-fill`, `onboarding-checkbox-border` |
`--dsw-alias-label-primary-foreground` (the label on primary buttons) is picked from black or white
by the accent's contrast, so it stays above 4.5:1 for any accent. Text tokens stay neutral (`#1a1d22
` / `#e6e8eb` primary).
The plugin also defines three tokens that the installed DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 still references but never de
clares (`--dsw-alias-bg-layer-4`, `--dsw-alias-bg-l1`, `--dsw-alias-bg-l2`), because the missing var
iables otherwise leave some backgrounds unresolved.
[该节后续省略]
### What is not tinted
Controls that already carry the DSH emphasis color keep it: `state-business-*` (focus borders, activ
e underlines, references), `button-info-*` (the send button), links, the dock drop indicator, and se
mantic success/warning/error and diff colors. Shiki syntax colors and the terminal ANSI palette also
rning/error and diff colors. Shiki syntax colors and the terminal ANSI palette also stay as shipped.
## API
Debug endpoint on the profile web server:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`GET /api/kde-tint/kde-colors` returns `200` with JSON:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
`accent` is `Colors:Selection.BackgroundNormal` from the applied `kdeglobals` (the live scheme Mater
ial You writes), not `General.AccentColor`, which often stays at an old manual value. `background`,
`view`, `button` and `tooltip` come from the matching `Colors:*` background entries and seed the sur
face ramp; they are `null` when the scheme does not define them. Values are normalized to `#rrggbb`
(the sources may use `#hex` or `r,g,b`).
`source` is `kdeglobals`, `scheme-file` (fallback to `~/.local/share/color-schemes` or `/usr/share/c
olor-schemes`) or `defaults`. `scheme` is `General.ColorScheme`. When the read fails, the response s
till returns `200` with the default values plus an `error` string. Unknown routes return `404`.

ent bundle is hand-written with no build step. Keep it that way.
